Pickled Herring

Served at: Noaptea Lupilor

Serves 6-8Prep 30 min (plus 2-3 days chilling)Cook 10 min

Noaptea Lupilor, or the Night of the Wolves, is a Romanian folk tradition observed around St. Andrew's Day (November 30th), a time when the veil between worlds is thin and protective rituals are common. While not a traditional Romanian dish for this specific night, pickled herring is a staple in many Eastern European cuisines, offering a robust and flavorful bite perfect for the colder, darker nights of late autumn. Its strong, pungent flavors can be seen as a hearty accompaniment to a night of vigil, providing warmth and sustenance.

Ingredients

  • 1 pound (450 g) fresh or previously frozen herring fillets, thawed if frozen
  • 1 large yellow onion, thinly sliced
  • 1 medium carrot, thinly sliced into rounds or julienned
  • 1 cup (240 ml) white vinegar (5% acidity)
  • 1 cup (240 ml) water
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 2 tablespoons (30 g) kosher salt
  • 1 tablespoon black peppercorns
  • 1 teaspoon mustard seeds
  • 2-3 bay leaves
  • 1/2 teaspoon allspice berries (optional)

Method

  1. If using fresh herring, clean and fillet the fish, removing any bones. If using frozen fillets, ensure they are fully thawed and pat them very dry with paper towels. Cut the herring fillets into 1-inch (2.5 cm) pieces.
  2. In a medium saucepan, combine the white vinegar, water, granulated sugar, kosher salt, black peppercorns, mustard seeds, bay leaves, and allspice berries (if using).
  3. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring until the sugar and salt are fully dissolved. Remove from heat and let the brine cool completely to room temperature.
  4. While the brine cools, prepare your vegetables. Thinly slice the yellow onion and the carrot.
  5. In a clean, sterile glass jar or non-reactive container, layer the herring pieces, sliced onion, and sliced carrot. Repeat layering until all ingredients are used, ending with a layer of vegetables.
  6. Once the brine is completely cool, pour it over the herring and vegetables in the jar, ensuring all ingredients are fully submerged. You may need to gently press down on the contents to ensure they are covered.
  7. Seal the jar tightly and refrigerate for at least 2-3 days before serving. The longer it marinates, the more the flavors will develop.
  8. Serve chilled, garnished with fresh dill if desired, alongside dark rye bread or boiled potatoes.

Tips

  • For a milder flavor, you can soak the herring pieces in milk for 1-2 hours before pickling, then rinse thoroughly and pat dry.
  • Experiment with other spices like juniper berries or a pinch of red pepper flakes for a spicier kick.
  • Pickled herring can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 2-3 weeks, ensuring it remains submerged in the brine.
